I promise that I don't usually do this, but I am going to share my experience with the fat acceptance movement because I never see anyone represent this perspective. I'm fat and have been trying not to be for years and years and years- since I was 10. I am now 24. I go down and up in the same 60 pound range. I have a 3.9 GPA, am well groomed, have a fiance with whom I have an awesome relationship, go to school full time and volunteer 20 hours per week. I DO care, I just have had some periods of very poor mental health that caused me to put on a lot of weight that I was afterwards unable to lose (I have a touch of the hypochondria and I feel so sick I can't function when my blood sugar is below about seventy or above about 90, so that makes it a lot harder to eat a low-calorie diet while dealing with other responsibilities).

It makes me feel better to find people who say that I DO deserve to live. My whole life isn't worthless just because I can't conquer this one problem, or because I haven't done it yet. There are other parts to being healthy, and other parts to being a person. The health at any size movement gave me the courage to exercise again, because you know what? I haven't failed if I don't manage to lose weight. My heart is still healthier, I'm still building muscle, and I'm still reaping the mental health benefits of getting outside and doing something.
